Yes — this is exactly the safety net I was hoping for. I opened the article, got the "this page can't be reached anymore" notice, and the saved copy still had the whole thing: the text was all there to read, the picture came through, and it still showed who wrote it and where it was originally published. So even though the live page is gone, I haven't actually lost what mattered — the content and the "where did this come from" details are preserved.

And I like that it happens quietly on its own when I first save, rather than me having to remember to press "save a copy." That's the whole point for me — I won't think to do it in the moment, so it needs to just happen.

I'm fine that the copy is the readable article rather than a fully working live version of the site — I don't need the buttons and interactive bits, I need the words and pictures to survive. That's the right trade.

This is the fallback I want. What's next?
